sample_en: He told me it would be wasted time to speak of business there, but that His Majesty would go within five or six days to Palencia, eight leagues away, where it would be easier to negotiate more fully.
why: Five folios (~6,600 words) of continuous French with about 190 [?] and 195 (?) marks (~6%); deciphered stretches in {braces}. Opening and middle build cleanly, the last page has several [?] and spaced-out letter fragments per sentence, so it reads in full but the end is thinner.

label: R1875, Sebastiano Foscarini, Escorial, 13 Oct 1761 (the chancery's decipherment)
sample_original: Le sciolte negoziazioni fra le Corti di Londra e di Versaglies sono la fonte da cui scaturiscono infinite congietture e sistemi politici.
sample_en: The broken-off negotiations between the courts of London and Versailles are the source of endless conjectures and political systems.
why: Chancery's own clean Italian decipherment transcribed with line breaks; no holes in the lines read, only editorial brackets for struck words.

label: R9658, RAH 9/26 ff. 371-376, Lope Hurtado de Mendoza, Rome, 23 Dec 1522 (CSP Spain ii no. 510)
sample_original: The Pope says he will not enter into a league with him (the Emperor) and the King of England as long as he has any hope of concluding a general peace.
sample_en: (already English calendar abstract)
why: A fluent English calendar abstract of the contemporary decipherment, complete but summarised in the third person; it is not our own word-by-word text.

label: Büchi 1925, no. 541
sample_original: Humanissimis suis ex Lundono 8. preteriti ad me datis litteris video moleste ferre, quod nec momenta occurrentiarum successuumque et bellicarum rerum nec cumulata Maj^ti V. quicquam obtulerim.
sample_en: From your most kind letters sent to me from London on the 8th of last month I see you take it ill that I have offered Your Majesty no news of events, successes and military affairs.
why: Full Latin letter (13 KB) as printed by Büchi, with the deciphered stretches marked and only 4 restored words; it is Büchi's published decipherment transcribed, not a new reading, but it reads fluently.

label: No. 18 (R4806), treaty articles subscribed by Niccolo Ziegler, [Pisa, Oct-Nov 1496]
file: lasry_report.md (full decryption and translation); transcripts/no18_reading.txt (project reading)
sample_original: Item q[uod] pro bono rei p[ublice] Sen[ensis] ÷ et [B]. illico manus apponerent ut saltem medietas illor[um] castrorum et arcium, ad que ipsi Senensibus ius competit, eis restituerentur
sample_en: Also that, for the good of the Sienese republic, [the League] should at once lend a hand so that at least half of those castles and strongholds to which the Sienese have a right be restored to them
why: Lasry's report gives the whole Latin decryption with a summary and a partial English translation, only a few unread signs; our own reading file is a line-by-line word list with ~12 open items per few lines (C on its own), but the Lasry text is what a reader would use.

label: R8416, Cotton Galba B V f. 40v, Spinelly to Henry VIII, Brussels, 1 Feb 1517
sample_original: audensier and misser loys de merlien the whiche audensier saythe that the [king] in the laterende of this wicke shall make his entree in to this town
sample_en: (already English, 16th-century spelling) Audensier and Messire Louis de Merlien, which Audensier says that the king will make his entry into this town at the end of this week
why: One continuous English sentence (the five cipher lines of the clear despatch) with two bracketed nomenclator words; short but reads fully, spelling needs modernising.

label: No. 6, BnF fr. 3022 ff. 16v-17v, del Vasto to Charles V, [Rome, early December 1527]
sample_original: creo mas presto sea esto porque segun la [dnh] no la seguiran en venir tan adelante no quedando en Lombardia exercito dellos tan pujante que pudiese resistir a una gruesa banda de alemanes
sample_en: I believe this will happen sooner, since they will not follow it by coming so far forward, with no army of theirs left in Lombardy strong enough to resist a large band of Germans
why: Current reading (98% of 1,680 tokens) is word-spaced Spanish with a few <[...]> and code-group holes; Lasry's prior file is letter-spaced with underscores (B alone); n6_reading.md carries the edited letter and a code table. Sentences build and translate.

label: R674, MNL OL E 199, Wesselényi's Latin draft, c. 1663-64
sample_original: Castrorum mutationes etiam necessariae essent, quo facto, si Dominus Generalis [60] regimenta Dominorum Haster, Snaidau et Spork coniungeret, possent ad minimum tria millia hominum constituere
sample_en: Changes of camp would also be necessary; this done, if the Lord General [60] joined the regiments of Messrs Heister, Schneidau and Sporck, they could make up at least three thousand men
why: Latin reading with an English translation in the same file; two code numbers ([60], [64]) are left open, the rest is complete. decode_out.txt is the raw decoder output and is not what is graded.
